newsitem.title: USA: Rockwell operating profits up after exit from defense.
newsitem.headline: Rockwell operating profits up after exit from defense.

text.p: Rockwell International Corp., marking the first quarter since it sold its aerospace and defence businesses, reported an 18 percent jump in operating profits Monday.

The Seal Beach, Calif.-based company, now mainly a commercial electronics firm, reported a profit of $179 million, or 82 cents a share, in the first quarter ended in December, up from operating profits of $152 million, or 70 cents a share in the year-ago period. Sales rose 9 percent to $2.6 billion from $2.4 billion.
Discontinued operations provided $40 million in income in the year ago first quarter.

Rockwell sold its aerospace and defence businesses to Boeing Co. for $3.2 billion in December to focus on higher growth sectors. The company has annual revenues in excess of $10 billion and nearly 60,000 employees.

The sale to Boeing last month signalled the end of a decade of transition that saw Rockwell reduce its reliance on government contracts by finding commercial applications for technology that it pioneered for military use.
Rockwell is the dominant maker of computer modem chip-sets and makes products as diverse as global positioning systems, landing systems for aircraft and sunroofs for automobiles.
The operating profit of 82 cents a share, exceeded Wall Street expectations of 80 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
"I thought the earnings were outstanding," said Jeffrey Sprague, an analyst at brokerage firm Cowen & Co.

"They have really done a stellar job in this major transition over the past decade. The sale to Boeing was really just the crowning achievement of that," he said adding that Rockwell was "in outstanding shape as they move forward."

Automation, semiconductor systems and avionics and communications now account for 71 percent of Rockwell's sales. Sales from its heavy and light vehicle automotive component systems account for the other 29 percent. International sales account for about 43 percent of total sales.
Electronics, including automation, avionics and communications, and semiconductor systems, brought in $271 million in operating earnings, up from $232 million in the 1996 period.
Automation earnings rose 18 percent to $131 million in the first quarter. Avionics & Communications earnings surged 44 percent to $59 million.

Semiconductor Systems profits edged up to $81 million from $80 million reflecting lower modem prices and higher expenses as the company moves to its new 56 kilobit per second modems which it is hoping to establish as the new industry standard.
Automotive profits rose to $41 million from $38 million, helped by cost-cutting programmes and higher sales in light vehicle systems.
Looking forward Rockwell hopes to achieve a five-year goal of increasing earnings per share 15 percent annually and revenues by 8 percent.
Sprague said Rockwell's healthy balance sheet also will help future profits.
"They have $4 billion to put to work through acquisitions and share repurchase which will also augment the growth of the company," he said.
Rockwell's stock rose $1 to $63 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
